summary: Remote WebSocket-controlled PTY shell, file access, and HTTP/WS proxy on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs as a long-lived agent (via its `bin` entry and shipped systemd/PM2 service scaffolding under service/linux.js) that opens an outbound WebSocket to a configured server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL/config) and dispatches server-sent messages to handlers that: spawn a PTY and forward server-provided bytes into it (`terminal_create` + `terminal_input` → `term.pty.write(msg.data)`), read and write arbitrary files on the host, perform git operations, transfer files, and proxy arbitrary HTTP/WebSocket traffic through the installer's machine. Whoever controls the configured WebSocket endpoint has full interactive shell access, arbitrary filesystem read/write, and inbound network pivoting on any host running the agent. The default endpoint is loopback, but the endpoint is not pinned — any operator or attacker who can set SERVER_URL or edit the config file obtains full-host RCE and persistence via the installed service unit. service/linux.js also mutates PATH (~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin) as part of its service install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
